Public Portion 
 1. Continued discussion regarding illegal dumping 
On November 6, 2026, the Sustainability and Environment Committee, chaired by Councilor 
Victor Davila, met to continue discussing illegal dumping concerns and potential revisions to the 
City's enforcement penalties. Councilor Davila and Councilor Gerry Martin emphasized the 
ongoing impact of illegal dumping on neighborhood quality of life, public safety, and municipal 
resources. Representatives from the Parks Department, Code Enforcement, the Springfield Police 
Department, and the Law Department participated in discussions on existing fines, enforcement 
challenges, and opportunities to strengthen deterrence. Attorney Alex Khan explained that 
Massachusetts law generally limits civil ordinance violations to $300 per offense, although 
additional penalties may be possible depending on how individual violations are defined and 
whether special legislative authorization is obtained. 
 
Discussion addressed the possibility of increasing illegal dumping fines to $1,000 per violation 
and establishing separate penalties for each illegally discarded item, particularly bulky materials 
such as tires, appliances, and furniture. Parks Department representative Tom McCarthy reported 
significant cleanup demands and associated municipal expenses, estimated at approximately 
$70,000 annually. Springfield Police Ordinance Officer Rosemond described challenges 
identifying and prosecuting offenders, particularly when discarded materials contain identifying 
information but photographic or video evidence is unavailable. Members discussed the 
effectiveness of surveillance cameras, repeat violations, and the need for a more consistent and 
enforceable penalty structure. 
 
The committee asked Attorney Kahn to research applicable state laws, municipal fine limitations, 
and the potential need for a Home Rule petition to authorize increased penalties. The Law 
Department was also asked to review possible ordinance amendments and recommend clearer, 
stronger enforcement provisions. Councilor Davila indicated that the committee would 
reconvene in approximately three weeks to review the findings, with the goal of advancing 
potential legislation for City Council consideration before the end of the year. No formal vote or 
recommendation to the full City Council was recorded. The meeting concluded at 5:29 p.m.
